projects.title: Smoothclean.ID Website
projects.summary: Designed and developed a premium service website for Smoothclean.ID, a Bandung-based shoe and leather care brand, from visual direction to frontend implementation and SEO article structure.
projects.impact: Turned a service business into a clearer digital experience with structured service categories, pricing, before-after proof, WhatsApp conversion paths, and SEO-ready educational articles.
projects.problem: Smoothclean.ID needed a sharper digital presence that could explain multiple care services, build trust, clarify pricing, and guide customers to order through WhatsApp without overwhelming them.
projects.goal: Create a clean, premium, conversion-focused website that presents shoe care, boots care, bag care, helmet care, leather jacket care, and baby gear cleaning in a structured and credible way.
users: Parents looking for baby gear cleaning
Bandung customers looking for pickup and delivery
process: Defined the website structure from hero, services, pricing, proof, workflow, testimonials, articles, and contact.
Created a visual direction that feels premium, clean, practical, and trustworthy for care services.
Designed service categories with clear treatment descriptions and estimated turnaround time.
Developed the frontend into a live responsive website.
Added SEO article structure to support organic search around shoe care, boots care, and baby gear cleaning topics.
Integrated WhatsApp CTA flow to make inquiries and orders easier.
solution: Premium landing page with strong headline and service positioning.
Six service category blocks for shoes, boots, bags, helmets, leather jackets, and baby gear.
Clear pricing section with estimated treatment cost and processing time.
Before-after result section to strengthen trust.
Three-step order flow: choose service, pickup/drop-off, receive notification.
SEO article section for educational content and search visibility.
projects.outcome: The website makes Smoothclean.ID easier to understand, easier to trust, and easier to contact. It also demonstrates my ability to combine UI/UX design, frontend development, SEO content structure, and business-oriented digital communication.

sections.title: From service complexity to clear information architecture
sections.body: The business covers many types of care services, so the main UX challenge was organizing them into a structure that users can scan quickly while still understanding the differences between each treatment.

sections.title: Designed for trust and conversion
sections.body: The website uses proof points such as operation year, customer rating, before-after visuals, clear pricing, testimonials, and pickup information to reduce hesitation before users contact via WhatsApp.

sections.title: SEO as part of the product experience
sections.body: Instead of treating articles as a separate blog, the article section is integrated as part of the customer education journey, helping users learn how to care for boots, sneakers, helmets, and baby gear.

projects.title: Palace Park POS System
projects.summary: A role-based POS concept created after observing that Palace Park still handled transaction counting manually.
projects.impact: Helps streamline cashier flow, reduce manual calculation errors, improve stock visibility, and give management clearer sales reporting.
projects.problem: Palace Park operations still relied on manual transaction counting and fragmented reporting, making sales, stock, and tenant performance harder to track accurately.
projects.goal: Design a simple POS system that helps cashiers record transactions faster, supports stock visibility, and gives management a clearer operational overview.
process: Observed manual sales calculation and reporting workflow.
Defined the need for faster cashier flow and clearer transaction records.
Mapped role-based access for super admin, tenant, cashier, and finance operations.
Designed core POS screens for sales, stock, receipts, and reporting.
Used an AI-assisted workflow with ChatGPT to accelerate planning, structure, and iteration.
solution: Role-based access for different operational needs.
POS transaction flow with menu selection, cart, payment method, and receipt structure.
Stock visibility so unavailable items can be marked and controlled.
Dashboard-ready sales data for total revenue, tenant performance, and payment breakdown.
projects.outcome: The concept transforms manual calculation into a structured digital workflow, reducing operational friction and making transaction records easier to review.

sections.title: Background
sections.body: The project started from a real operational observation: sales calculation was still handled manually. This created a need for a lightweight POS experience that could be used by multiple roles without making the workflow complicated.

sections.title: Design Direction
sections.body: The interface prioritizes speed, clarity, and role-based simplicity. The core experience focuses on cashier flow, menu availability, receipt output, and simple reporting.

sections.title: AI-assisted Workflow
sections.body: ChatGPT was used to structure product logic, define role permissions, break down features, and accelerate iteration while keeping design decisions grounded in the operational problem.

projects.title: Phinter HRIS Mobile UI/UX
projects.summary: Mobile-first HRIS experience for attendance, leave requests, company news, and employee administrative tasks.
projects.impact: Simplified daily HR workflows and supported faster handoff through reusable components.
projects.problem: Legacy HR workflows were difficult to manage, causing friction in attendance tracking, leave requests, and employee communication.
projects.goal: Transform complex HR workflows into a seamless mobile-first experience with clear navigation and accessible UI for employees aged 25–50.
process: Align HR utility and stakeholder branding
projects.outcome: The simplified attendance flow reduced user friction and the design system enabled faster handoff to development.

sections.title: Design Challenge
sections.body: The interface needed to balance HR utility, executive aesthetic preferences, corporate credibility, and accessibility.

sections.title: Impact
sections.body: The final direction gained stakeholder approval and improved clarity for attendance, company news, and administrative tasks.

projects.title: MECS Website Redesign
projects.summary: Corporate website redesign to modernize the brand image, improve hierarchy, and clarify services for B2B users.
projects.impact: Elevated corporate credibility through cleaner layout, stronger hierarchy, and clearer CTA structure.
projects.problem: The previous website felt static, outdated, and lacked strong hierarchy, making service communication less clear for B2B decision makers.
projects.goal: Modernize the corporate website while keeping the brand credible, formal, and aligned with stakeholder expectations.
projects.outcome: The redesign improved perceived professionalism, clarified services, and helped the company present a more credible digital presence.

sections.title: Core Challenge
sections.body: Different stakeholders had different visual preferences, so the design needed to balance bold modern visuals and conservative corporate expectations.

sections.title: Learning
sections.body: Stakeholder alignment is crucial in corporate projects because structure and clarity often define perceived professionalism.

projects.title: APTA Living Social Media Strategy
projects.summary: Localized social media strategy across Bali, BSD, and Pekanbaru using Instagram paid campaigns and TikTok organic content.
projects.impact: Improved engagement through hook and retention optimization, strengthened regional positioning, and increased responsiveness.
projects.problem: A furniture brand needed localized content strategies across Bali, BSD, and Pekanbaru while maintaining efficient Instagram ads and organic TikTok engagement.
projects.goal: Improve engagement, strengthen brand positioning, and tailor content based on audience behavior in each showroom region.
process: Optimize CTR, CPC, engagement, and retention
projects.outcome: The strategy improved content relevance, strengthened regional positioning, and increased responsiveness across social platforms.

sections.title: Market Segmentation
sections.body: The strategy separated audience needs by showroom: Bali for premium villa and expat context, BSD for residential and F&B use, and Pekanbaru for value-driven messaging.

sections.title: Optimization
sections.body: Content was refined through hooks, retention signals, CTR, CPC, engagement, and audience interaction.

projects.title: Company-wide Design System
projects.summary: Reusable components and standards to unify UI consistency across web and mobile products.
projects.impact: 30% faster design-to-development handoff and clearer implementation standards across product teams.
projects.problem: UI components and implementation patterns needed stronger consistency across web and mobile products.
projects.goal: Create reusable components, visual standards, and documentation that improve product consistency and developer handoff.
projects.outcome: The design system reduced handoff time by 30% and improved UI consistency across product teams.

sections.title: System Audit
sections.body: The process began by identifying inconsistent interface patterns and handoff gaps across product teams.

sections.title: Impact
sections.body: The system helped teams work faster, reduce ambiguity, and keep UI quality more consistent across platforms.
